validator.sign.title: Sign your validator authorization
validator.sign.intro: Keep your wallet on this device. Sign here, then take the signature back to the computer running your validator.
validator.sign.loadTitle: 1. Load the message from your validator
validator.sign.privacy: The file is read on this device and is not uploaded. Your wallet receives the authorization only when you choose to sign.
validator.sign.reviewTitle: 2. Check the wallet and validator keys
validator.sign.permission: These keys can sign daily TDH results. This does not send a transaction, cost gas, or let them move NFTs or funds.
validator.sign.replace: This authorization replaces the previous authorization from this wallet when it takes effect. Only the keys listed here will remain authorized by it.
validator.sign.revoke: This message lists no keys. Signing it revokes this wallet’s validator authorization when it takes effect.
validator.sign.confirm: I exported this message from my validator and checked every key and share against the Validator app.
validator.sign.confirmRevoke: I exported this message from my validator and intend to revoke this wallet’s validator authorization.
validator.sign.notConnected: Connect the wallet shown above to continue.
validator.sign.mismatch: The connected wallet does not match the wallet in this message. Switch to {address} to sign.
validator.sign.safe: This flow requires a wallet that can produce a standard Ethereum signature. Safe and other smart contract wallets are not supported.
validator.sign.walletHelp: On a phone, use your wallet’s browser or choose your wallet in the connection window. Review the authorization there before signing.
validator.sign.returnTitle: 3. Return the signature to your validator
validator.sign.success: Signature ready. Your validator is not authorized until you submit it in the Validator app.
validator.sign.returnHelp: On the validator computer, paste this into the signature field under Another device or a signing tool and choose Send the signature. Use the same message you exported.
validator.sign.copyError: Could not copy automatically. Select and copy the signature below.
validator.sign.pending: Finish or cancel the request in your wallet before starting another one.
validator.sign.error.invalid: This is not a supported validator authorization. Export grant.json from your Validator app and try again.
validator.sign.error.tooLarge: This file is too large. Choose the grant.json file exported by your Validator app (up to 64 KB).
validator.sign.error.network: This message is for a different validator network. This page supports the 6529 main network only.
validator.sign.error.keys: The message contains invalid or duplicate keys or shares. Export a new grant.json from your Validator app.
validator.sign.error.read: Could not read this file. Try choosing it again or paste its contents.
validator.sign.error.sign: The wallet could not sign this authorization. Try again with a wallet that supports EIP-712 typed data.
validator.sign.error.rejected: Signing was canceled. Nothing was submitted. You can try again.
validator.sign.error.changed: The wallet connection changed while signing. Reconnect the wallet named in the message and try again.
validator.sign.error.signature: The returned signature does not match the wallet in the message. Nothing was submitted. Reconnect the correct wallet and try again.
validator.sign.error.connect: Could not open the wallet connection. Please try again.
validator.sign.linkBody: Export grant.json from the Validator app, then sign it on the device where you keep your wallet.
validator.sign.loadHint: Choose the grant.json file saved by your Validator app.
validator.sign.helpOpenTitle: Open the Validator app on the node computer
validator.sign.helpOpen: At the Authorize step, expand Another device or a signing tool under Other ways to sign.
validator.sign.helpSave: Enter the address of the wallet you want to authorize the validator with, then choose Save the message. The app saves a file called grant.json.
validator.sign.helpTransferTitle: Bring that file to your wallet device
validator.sign.helpTransfer: Transfer grant.json to this phone or computer, then choose it below. You can also copy the file’s contents and use Or paste the file contents.
validator.sign.helpNote: Keep the Validator app on that authorization screen. After signing here, you’ll paste the signature back there.
validator.sign.walletMatch: Connected wallet address matches this authorization.
